Formulation
This patient's asthma flare-up appears to be precipitated by increased pollen exposure or a viral infection. Previous history of asthma during childhood requiring hospitalization, along with hay fever and eczema, are significant perpetuating factors. The presence of a supportive partner is a noted protective factor.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Asthma flare-up
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve symptom relief and manage asthma effectively
- Clinical Goal(s): Stabilize asthma symptoms and prevent future exacerbations
- Actions (Patient): Use spacer with inhaler, follow up with a peak flow meter measurement, record peak flow values daily
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe a peak flow meter and spacer, review patient’s asthma management in one week, recommend regular antihistamine use

Secondary Problem: Viral infection (suspected)
- Patient Goal(s): Recover from suspected viral infection
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor and manage symptoms of viral infection if confirmed
- Actions (Patient): Monitor symptoms; contact clinician if conditions worsen
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide advice if symptoms of viral infection exacerbate

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Asthma management, use of spacer and peak flow meter
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased wheezing, high temperature
- Coping Strategies: Utilize prescribed inhaler techniques, take antihistamines
